quest.title: Tracing the Footsteps of the Past
quest.description: Beneath the moon's watchful light, everyone is marching to the conclusions of their own stories...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1325, Primogem x30, Mora x58200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VII
chapter.title: A Traveler on a Winter's Night

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Aaagh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It appears that The Doctor's energy signature has changed to something similar to kuuvahki — but not like the kuuvahki we're used to.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Nod-Krai's kuuvahki devices will only have a limited effect on it. I can see why you've chosen to place your hopes in alchemy instead.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Also... I must say, these books are rather profound...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: My subordinates just shipped them in from Fontaine. Some of them are from the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, some are incident reports from Petrichor, and then there's a few test reports for these junk machines. Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Additionally, after some further scanning I've discovered something extremely annoying.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Teyvat's skies contain multiple moons. A long time ago, when I did my first scan, I detected three — just as the legends say.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But when I checked again just now, I detected four moons.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So there's one extra?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah. Originally, I thought that if I could still find three moons, that would at least mean Columbina's still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But then it occurred to me that apart from the Frost Moon, Teyvat's moons are just husks.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And husks surely shouldn't show up in the scan, since they're not alive.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's weird, isn't it? If we can't even distinguish between a dead and a living moon, how are we supposed to know whether a Moon Goddess is still alive?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Or does this mean that the Moon Marrows are equivalent to the moons themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's certainly possible. In which case, the fourth moon you detected may be Dottore's artificial creation.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So he wasn't bluffing. He really built his own Moon Marrow... Ugh, I'm so mad right now.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's easy to get overwhelmed when you have too much on your plate. Maybe you need to relax? Perhaps try going for a walk, or simply take a few deep breaths.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Nothing can calm me down at a time like this. I need more time, and I need progress.

dialogues.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
dialogues.text: Dodo! Dodo! Dodoco!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm? It's Mr. Flins.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I really hate that ringing noise... Ugh! First the Four Orthants of the Narzissenkreuz, then Moon Marrows... Now what!?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry if we're disturbing you. Might I ask what's troubling you?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What do you want? We're busy.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Are you still at the Curatorium of Secrets?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah? Look, everyone else is still out, so there's no hurry. Plus, I'm busy, so I would appreciate if you gave me some space.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Even though we have crucial intel to share?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. Fine, I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Do you intend to share it via the Dodocommunication Device?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Ordinarily I would, but this is a unique situation. I think it's best that we discuss it in person. See you at the Curatorium.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright then. So what's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The rest of the team is still out working on their missions and evacuations, but we've decided to fill you in on the most crucial information first.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sandrone, you were right... Columbina is most likely still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's the best news we've received in a while, by a long way.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Flins and Nefer share the information they found, and what they think it implies...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Random locations... appearing in reverse order? Are you serious? Ugh. So not dying isn't enough for the Moon Goddess, huh? She has to show off too?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Anyway, does this mean we can deduce her condition from the Moon Marrows?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Miss Sandrone, there's nothing wrong with simply admitting that you're happy to hear the good news.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm not! And she's the least of our problems! We're facing a huge crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If she can't control the flow of time in there, she's just gonna keep moving backwards. Different points in time won't intersect, and she'll never find a way out.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Let's say life begins with a drop of water... When did time begin? The moment this planet came into being?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No, that's not right. Her final destination would be the moment at which the space she is in was created.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But it doesn't seem like we can influence that space from the outside world. So, how can we help her?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Also, if she's alive, Rerir and Tholindis might be too — but as far as we know, neither of them have come back out... That space may not have an exit at all.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I must concur with Miss Nefer in this.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Can't exactly argue with that. Let's leave it there for now — I've taken notes on everything you said.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Will it help with your research?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I doubt it's gonna help with breaking Dottore's energy fields. But who knows when it might come in handy? Better to have it all written down than try to remember everything when I need it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, I need to get back to my research. Mr. Albedo has made a lot of suggestions that will require my undivided attention.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sure. I'll stay here. I have things to work on.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Paimon, are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #Oh, right — she went with Varka to Natlan, didn't she? Good thing we've moved her and {NICKNAME}'s luggage in here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #Speaking of {NICKNAME}... where could they be...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm? There's a note... from Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: #Paimon here. Not in at the moment, but if anyone needs to borrow her stuff, or {NICKNAME}'s, go ahead and help yourself. Paimon won't be mad!

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: #Also, {NICKNAME}: If you get back before Paimon, make sure to get some rest. Paimon misses you a lot, but put your health first, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hah. How sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, since you offered, Paimon, don't mind if I do...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #(This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon's luggage. All the items they use day-to-day are here.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (It's well organized. I wonder which of them is responsible for that?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What do we have here?

dialogues.speaker: Observe Luggage
dialogues.text: (Among the daily necessities, there's a photo.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (The Kamera captured a special moment that can only occur between people who are close to one another.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (You can really sense how the photographer feels about their subject. I wonder why this picture was placed outside? Is it because Paimon recently looked at it?)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Luggage
dialogues.text: #(There's also a thick Adventure Handbook in here — a record of {NICKNAME}'s achievements and memories in Teyvat.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #This must belong to {NICKNAME}... Perfect. I'll use this.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Hang in there. We'll find you.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Let's see, this one is... "Automnequi Sermon Dictation: Concerning the Apocalypse."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "I believe that the correct term for this is 'Fortuna.' This was an ancient Remurian technology, a wisdom unparalleled."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "...I never imagined that Remurian ideas would be so similar to the diagram I have named the 'world-formula.' This is strong evidence that..."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Human civilization should gradually shed possibilities as it continues to explore and evolve... The end of humankind may well be upon us right now..."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "The sparks of civilization shall run out unless we consider introducing variables from outside the system."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Variables"? Surely that can only mean one thing?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Descenders?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: #Dottore likely captured {NICKNAME} because of {M#his}{F#her} Descender status. But the three moons' authority comes from the world itself. Why would Dottore need anything beyond that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Where does this "variable" factor in? The world-formula calculates the fate of an entire world. Introducing a variable would therefore give us...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Automnequi Sermon Dictation: Explications on the Chymical Marriage"... These titles are pretty esoteric...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Observe and compute the pathway displayed in the guidance diagram. Deconstructing and reversing its effects could generate potential ideas..."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So it's one of Rene's draft lectures? Deconstructing the pathway... Hmm, I suppose that could lead to a breakthrough.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Most of the experimental devices proposed by the Liliacruces Ordo are built based on the simple and basic logical structure of a tree model..."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Liliacruces... Guess they were trying to cover up the name of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "When Duke St. Germanus departed, he said, 'It seems that there's no going back.' Alas, he is only a genius when it comes to machines..."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "In all other things, he is but ordinary." ... Excuse me? I'm sorry, that's just ridiculous. What kind of book is this?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Great Detective Hurlock: The Alchemist and the Clockwork Saint"!? Isn't this a novel? Come on...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Still, the author swears that they knew Rene well... Whatever. I guess it's not beyond the realms of possibility that Rene would say nonsense like that on occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Memory, wishes, souls, and persona... Frankly, this sounds more like occultism, but if Albedo vouches for it, I suppose there must be some alchemical basis to these techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The way Alain Guillotin saw it, the world was comprised of machines. The universe needed machines, and thus his technologies were created. That's why I was born.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Rene... His full name was Rene de Petrichor, if I recall correctly. Sounds like he and the town must be intricately connected.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That place was also the source of most of our information regarding Remurian civilization. Seems like some of his projects were based on their technology.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The cutting of souls and storing them in vessels... These seemingly unrelated techniques underpinned Rene's research. Assuming that the Four Orthants correspond to alchemical categories...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The Chymical Marriage model? Alain would've scoffed at that. He never would have let those theories or parameters anywhere near his mathematical formulas.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh... Cookies to go with the tea? Let's see... They must be from that person who brought those documents. I see they're from Hotel Debord.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Something's written on the box... "We are proud to present this homage to the Fortress of Meropide's fun-filled meal collection system: Fortune Cookies! Have a lucky start to your day!"

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Sounds like a dumb gimmick to me... Hmm? "Be early to bed and early to rise, get plenty of sun and drink plenty of water. Then, things will surely go well for you"...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What? Are you kidding me? Somehow, I doubt that an early night and a glass of water is magically gonna save a world on the brink of existential peril.

dialogues.speaker: Illki
dialogues.text: Lady Arlecchino. Word has reached us that Lady Marionette's troops are all in position. They are ready to act as soon as the order is given.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Excellent.

dialogues.speaker: Illki
dialogues.text: The only thing is, they are fewer in number than we expected... It looks like many of them must have lost their lives at the hands of the monsters released by The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Can't be helped. Allow them to join our ranks, and keep in contact.

dialogues.speaker: Illki
dialogues.text: As you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Arlecchino. You look well.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Did Dottore really have to build his lab right on the sole path between Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai? I had to go on a huge detour to stay out of its line of sight.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Sounds like an arduous journey. I assume you've brought word from Her Majesty?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Of course. All part of the job.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Firstly, the Tsaritsa has authorized Fatui Inte{RUBY#[D]Okhranka}rnal Affairs to review Dottore's case. They will reach a formal verdict on whether he has turned traitor and whether he poses a threat to Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: While they're working on that, I've been ordered to come and receive the refugees from Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: They are nearby. My team will escort you to them shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Great.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Aside from that, Her Majesty has a message for you and Sandrone personally... Huh? Where's Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: She stayed behind to work since I was making the trip anyway. It seemed sensible to have one person on standby at base while the other came out to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Alright, guess that's just how she rolls. In that case, tell her that the Tsaritsa's decree this time is pretty awesome-sounding. I think she'll like this one.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Still, I wonder why... Wait, what's that?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Did one of our troops... turn into a monster?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Take him out.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: I can't believe it. He was a living, breathing human one moment, and the next...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Another fine piece of work by our dear colleague, I'm afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: ...What in the world has been going on in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: A lot. But long story short, Dottore stole two Moon Marrows that should have belonged to Columbina, then built a third Moon Marrow of his own to concentrate the tri-lunar authority in his hands.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: What!? What do you mean, he built a moon marrow? People build roads and houses, not moon marrows... What's his next DIY project? He's gonna build a god?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You could stand to be less surprised. We are Harbingers — the work we are engaged in makes the creation of gods seem mundane by comparison.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I tell everyone who asks that you once crossed swords with Rex Lapis while serving as a key supporter for Rosalyne's plan... But right now, you're acting like a common adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Haha, thanks for speaking up for me. Those two really took me for a ride back then...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Then again, surely no common adventurer would manage to get tangled up with them the way I did... That's gotta count in my favor, right?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: It almost sounds like you wish to repeat the experience. I might have to lower my opinion of you.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Uh, no, no, no! I'll stop talking, hehe. Please, go on.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Dottore is currently still experimenting with his newfound power in ways that continue to corrode the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: As for the human mutation, I believe this is simply a consequence of his experiments, and not a strategic move.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That Radiant Beast was once a subordinate of Sandrone's. I suspect he was only allowed to live so that he could become an experimental subject.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Also, those of us who fought Dottore have been afflicted with a curse. As such, I cannot leave Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: This is so much worse than I thought... No wonder Her Majesty's decree is so extreme.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: "While these exceptional circumstances persist, the Harbingers are hereby authorized to use unilateral executive powers. Should Dottore pose a threat, Arlecchino and Sandrone are permitted to eliminate him."

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: My thanks to Her Majesty. I will pass these good tidings on to Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Her Majesty has also declared that she will refrain from launching an attack on the now-evacuated Nod-Krai, due to the presence of unretrieved research material.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: A wise decision.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: By the way, how's my old partner doing? I'm assuming they're with you?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #Partner? You mean {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #I'm afraid I have bad news. {M#He}{F#She} was captured after our failed assault on Dottore's lab. {M#His}{F#Her} whereabouts are currently unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: #What!? Why? Since when does Dottore have a bone to pick with {M#him}{F#her}?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That is indeed the question. I'm not sure he does. He must have some other goal in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: #This won't do. I have to rescue {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #You can't. We have no idea where {NICKNAME} is.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Ugh... What am I supposed to do, then? Stand here twiddling my thumbs?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Sandrone is working on it. The best thing you can do right now is complete your mission.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: ...Fine. I guess I'll... leave this to you, then.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: One last thing. Tell The Rooster to get the message out to the gods and citizens of every nation in Teyvat: Beware, an uncontrollable pollution is spreading forth from Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The source of that pollution is a madman drunk on the success of his experiments. The Fatui and our allies will endeavor to contain the threat.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: However, if Nod-Krai falls, things are likely to escalate.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Considering Dottore is one of our own, all Fatui stationed in Nod-Krai consider it our duty to stay and fight him to the bitter end, whatever the cost.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Hey, don't be too pessimistic. If it comes to it, I'm sure Her Majesty won't stand by and do nothing.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I hope you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You're right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thanks. Hey, do you think I'll get that gliding exam exemption?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I made sure I was on my best behavior in Mondstadt. I landed well outside the city and walked in through the gates...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll help you apply, don't worry. For now, let's see what we have here.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What are The Doctor's energy fields even made from? The usual attract and repel principles that govern kuuvahki don't seem to apply to them.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: They are very mysterious, but ultimately, they appear to be comprised of energies from the three realms.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thanks to research by Master and the Hexenzirkel, we know that Teyvat's seven elements are derived from the more primordial power of the Light Realm, which is antagonistic with the power of the Void Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since you have the power of the dragon Durin within you, I'm sure you can already tell that this energy field contains no Abyssal energy.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...That's true. It's not Abyssal energy... it's something pure, wild and untamed.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I've been thinking about something. Do you still remember the device that Dori supplied from the Akademiya when you and Miss Columbina fought Rerir?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That was one of the most marvelous feats of ingenuity I've ever seen. The design, the craftsmanship, the material selection... I couldn't fault any of it.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Not to mention the operating principles — surely the most ingenious feature of all. Dori didn't go into detail on how it functions, but I have a working theory.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The clue was that Miss Columbina was somehow able to use the Pyro energy that you provided — despite the fact that, as a Moon Goddess, she should only be able to use Light Realm energy in principle.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Now, all elemental energy is, of course, derived from Light Realm energy to begin with. Hence, I suspect that the device works by restoring elemental energy to its original state.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This presumes a theoretical model of the seven elements akin to that of light refracted through a prism... Perhaps it is no mere analogy. Maybe there is indeed a prism in this model.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I almost wonder if the idea for the device was conceived based on direct observations of said prism? It would explain how such an ironclad design concept was achieved.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It is at once a masterwork of engineering and a groundbreaking application of the Akademiya's latest elemental theories.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I suspect only Lesser Lord Kusanali herself could have devised such an ambitious technology.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But back to the energy field before us. If this is pure Light Realm energy, its relation to elemental energy is one of integration versus division — or you could say that the former contains the latter.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Could this mean that elemental energy can dilute the power of the Light Realm?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Should we give it a try?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We should.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It works!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Clear signs of disruption were detected at the periphery of the energy field. This indicates that elemental energy can disturb or even negate the field.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Now you try.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Alright, here goes...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's working...!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Switch to Abyssal energy and attack again.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hah!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No surprises there. Abyssal power drains the energy field to a significantly greater extent...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I now feel confident in asserting that the energy field is indeed pure Light Realm energy, and that elemental energy can dilute it.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But the energy field is huge... how much elemental energy will it take to neutralize it?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We don't have to neutralize it completely. We can try other approaches.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's all for theory. Would you like to continue watching?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So you knew I was here.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Huh? When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: A while ago. But Albedo sounded like he was working on his thesis defense back there. Back in Sumeru, you can end a person's whole career by interrupting them mid-speech.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Very thoughtful of you — I'm truly touched. Could I ask you to lend me a hand?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: With what?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A little test. Try using Anemo to unleash a concentrated assault with circular blades, with the goal of breaking through at a singular point.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Nice! This time, it tore through the field!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Tremendous. This is a major breakthrough.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Should we go through?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We probably shouldn't risk having mutually antagonistic energies in such close proximity... Durin, you stay here and watch the entrance. Hat Guy and I will go in to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sounds sensible to me. Keep your eyes peeled, Durin.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I've got this. You two be careful in there. Just give me the signal if you need help, and I'll dive right in.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "signal"?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's based on a new alchemical concoction I developed last month. When two bottles of it are smashed on the ground together, they emit a blinding burst of light. If it comes to that, remember to shield your eyes with your hat.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Glad I asked. Thanks for the heads-up.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: They have no heartbeat and they're not breathing... We can only assume they're dead. But there are no visible wounds...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Also, there's an animal squatting next to each body.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...It's watching us. That's not an animal's gaze.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What are you trying to tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Doesn't seem eager to talk... I guess maybe it is just an animal after all.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Let's keep looking around.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Same situation everywhere. Not a living soul in sight... just countless bodies with animals standing watch over them.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well... I think we can safely rule out the possibility that they're all pets.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Is skirting around the topic your way of showing consideration for other people's feelings?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Just being cautious. I don't doubt that you can handle the truth.
Please... help us... Please...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What happened here?
...I don't know... Suddenly, everyone collapsed... Then my line of sight got... lower...
I still... have some of my senses left... I gotta... get out of here... I... Ah, aah...
*cheep*

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It looks like there's a huge experiment going on inside this energy field.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Maybe each energy field is its own giant experiment... Ugh. Vile.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: He's swapping human minds with those of animals... Even without the other circumstances, this would still be an extremely radical experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Those people may have lost their sense of selves, but they are not fully animals either. If they were, they would have left — but instead, their instincts are driving them to remain by their dead bodies.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We should go. No sense in sticking around here longer than we need to.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You're back! Everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We saw some things that take a strong stomach. Otherwise, we're fine.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We should share our findings with the others.

dialogues.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
dialogues.text: Dodo! Dodo! Dodoco!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes? Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Miss Nefer, it's me, Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We've found a way to break through the energy fields. With enough control, it's possible to tear them open using elemental energy.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Also, we managed to take a look inside. Dottore is carrying out his cruel experiments on an immense scale. Any residents who have failed to evacuate in time will likely meet a grisly end.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sounds like he's living down to our expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Might I ask how things are proceeding on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm just about to get started. I'll be in touch once I have a result.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Understood. Stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, Nefer, I'll link up with you once my tasks are complete.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What makes you think I'd need you to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'll need it. And considering the way you approach certain matters, I think you'll be better off with me present.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's begin. Entering simulation mode...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #(A vast wasteland. Is this {NICKNAME}'s inner world?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...I was expecting something more vibrant, to be honest.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Wait. Someone's there...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you looking at?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll look at it with you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to know all about everything you've seen and experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Is there somewhere I should return to? Or should I stay here and be the hero everyone says I am?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't dislike my current life. Roaming the land, fighting battles, accomplishing missions, earning a living, looking after Paimon... It's not so bad.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess the only thing that's missing is that... you're not here with me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (This is the conscious layer, which contains a person's true feelings. It is filled with both longing and kindness.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...I suppose anyone who lives long enough ends up wishing for someone who can't be there. Maybe it's the only way we can feel truly alive.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Time to delve a little deeper...)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Nasha Town is hardly the optimal choice for a place to live, but it has character, and a reasonable population density.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Oh, don't be nervous. I was just thinking where might make a good starting point for your journey.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should send you further afield. Khaenri'ah, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ah ceased to exist long ago.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Once again, you fail to understand the possibilities that the Trilune creates. Anything that has existed in the past, I can now recreate.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You simply do not wish to see that happen. That might be because you miss your sibling and fear getting answers that you are not ready to learn... but this is not for me to judge.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: If we are to collaborate, we need to maintain an amicable relationship. In a moment, you will be able to...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Oh no!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you gonna do?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Don't move.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Something unwanted has crept into... Oh? Gone as quickly as it came.

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror
Enter the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I've entered the past three times at this point, but I still have so many questions...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (For instance, beyond each point being further back in time than the last, what determines the specific locations at which I can make entry?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #(So far, the common thread linking all three scenarios is that {NICKNAME} has been present...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #(But it's more than that. I know I sensed something familiar around {M#him}{F#her}... What was it?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I'll keep this question in mind as I carry on...)
Hey... Wake up.
Hey! Did you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbina! I said, wake up! Now!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? Oh. Good morning, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's three in the afternoon, actually... And could you kindly not use my quarters as your personal nap room next time?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Aw... But I feel so safe here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And your... coffee, right? It's so bitter, but it smells lovely.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah, it's like you were raised by wolves in a forest or something. What did you drink growing up? Grass tea?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Scions certainly lead a more frugal existence than the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Then I'll bet you've never eaten one of these before!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...It smells delicious.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's because it's a Fontainian recipe. I had a little free time today, so I made a batch.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Rosalyne will be here shortly, but if you really can't wait, I guess you can go ahead and—

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: *munching*

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey! At least let me finish before you start eating! Did the Frostmoon Scions not teach you basic table manners!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Or did the rules not apply to you, because you're the high and mighty Moon Goddess?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mmm... These are so tasty.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Of course they are. I made them.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I was worried they might contain traces of machine oil.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Y'know, there's something I've always wanted to ask you. Why did you leave your old home and join the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I mean, I'm sure their food was awful. But there's gotta be more to it than that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well... Life there didn't go quite how I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What were you expecting? You're a god. Your followers are gonna make some demands of you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Surely you can just answer a few prayers here and there in return for the free food and drink? How bad can it be?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well... Would you help other people, just for free food and drink?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Doctor told me that you were created by a great mechanic... Lord Something-Fisher...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The "Lord-Artificer"... Bah, some people can't keep their mouths shut...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, Lord-Artificer. And didn't he have something to do with the, uh, narcissist...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes, that was it. Narzissenkreuz Ordo. So, would you try to fulfill their wishes?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You must be joking. I wouldn't go even if they paid me — I don't even know them.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Exactly. Well, I felt the same way. I did not know the people who made demands of me.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh. What do you know? We're on the same page for once.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: In his later years, Alain did ask me if there was anything I wanted to do — if I had wishes of my own. Hmph, well, I don't. And I'm not in any mood to fulfill someone else's, either.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Who's Alain?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: He was the... You know what? Never mind. You're not gonna remember. Anyway, the point I'm trying to make is, neither of us is the self-sacrificing type.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Lemme ask you this. What sort of place would you like to live in if you could choose?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... A place where people don't ask me for things I cannot give them. Where they don't worship me, or fear me, but just want to chat with me like a normal person...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd also like the freedom to come and go as I please. And ideally, it would be somewhere with the smell of coffee and snacks...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah. Not to burst your bubble, but no such place exists in the world. Now, take your snacks and scram!

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror
Enter the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (The Final Night Cemetery... This is where Flins is based.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Or not! How are we supposed to read through this many files!?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Difficult, yes, but it is also our most efficient option.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Seems like they're searching for information... Oh, I remember. Flins and Varka talked about some files on the Wild Hunt...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Was this my doing, too?)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: To expose the true intentions of this Rerir, we need to dive into Nod-Krai's history.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Are my actions changing the past... or are they simply completing a process?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is all of this inevitable? Or am I the one making these decisions?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (If I choose not to help them now, will it change how things turn out?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Hope we don't land on our heads, then...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Haha... They're my friends. I can't not help them...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! Gh—Ghost!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (And the other one was... here.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, another file's moving!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (That should do it...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Luonnotar?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You... can sense my presence?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...! Wait!

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: How would you like to experience the thrill of never being held accountable for your actions? You could crush people like ants without consequence. Or tear off their heads, or limbs, as you please.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Believe me, such a life is but one small step away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What point is he trying to make? Freedom? But... the freedom to kill? To do evil and get away with it?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would you offer me that?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: The creation of a world is the ultimate scientific experiment. I have taken my research to the highest level, where I shall be not just a god, but also a servant to many sacred spirits. I shall heed the truth and perform holy deeds.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: A god's laboratory is the perfect playground — but it needs the right occupant to explore its full potential.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Mortals are found everywhere one looks. Not so with Descenders. I'd prefer my first guest to be a distinguished individual such as yourself, and I know you could make the most of the opportunities it offers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So the condition for entering the new world is to take innocent lives. The same dilemma that Rerir once faced.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Could I really bring myself to kill others for my own benefit? Rerir did... and look where it got him.)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Have you made up your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't do it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your playground is no place for me — you're putting your hopes in the wrong person. But we both know I'm not quite the hero you say I am either. I have my own reasons for the journey I'm on, and they aren't all selfless.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You've grown a lot since we last met, but there are still things you are unwilling to compromise on. This will only hinder you.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Why don't I lower my requirements a little, as a gesture of goodwill? I'll give you a little time to learn to be a less noble soul. That'll make things much easier for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I... I really doubt I could live that sort of life.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: And yet you already sound less defiant than a moment ago. The benefits appeal to you, because you can read the signs of the times.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Why don't we return to my research facility? Your last visit was so rushed. There is much that I have yet to show you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: *panting*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hat Guy? How did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You're still gonna call me "Hat Guy" after that, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You came all this way just to save me?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I didn't see anyone else in there who needed saving.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Ugh... *cough*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, you're injured?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It's nothing. I'll be fine.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Why are you looking at me like that? Is it that shocking that I'd come to your rescue?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm more shocked that you caught The Doctor off guard...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I owed you a favor from back in Sumeru. Now, we're even.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Distracting Dottore was tough, I won't lie...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: He's not gonna fall for the same trick twice. That was my one shot... I'd hoped to use it to take him out.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Ugh. I never wanted to obliterate someone more than I do right now.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Dottore doesn't recognize me, but his Segments were originally made based on an analysis of my operational principles.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I expect it's only a matter of time before he figures out what I am.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(So Dottore doesn't recognize {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}, because he deleted himself from Irminsul.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...Did he really miss his only chance for revenge by saving me?)

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Why the long face? Hey, I'm not blaming you, okay?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: And I'm not complaining either. Rescuing you and killing Dottore are equally important goals.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Everyone would be pretty stuck without you. It's best you live to fight another day.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: How are you holding up? Are you alright?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hat Guy said to put safety first, so we agreed to run as far away as we could after leaving the energy field, and only meet up once it was safe.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: You don't look injured. It seems that Dottore didn't do anything to you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, I'm fine, guys. Thanks.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Alright, rescue operation complete. Let's head back.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: There's a lot more work to be done before this is over.

choices.text: Fair point. You just caught me by surprise... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: You've gotten stronger, Arlecchino! Nice!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Stop that right now.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I appreciate the praise, but I am not fighting you today.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: *sigh* I knew it...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Like I thought... beyond a certain distance, we can't see the opening where we came in. Maybe that's to prevent people from escaping?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sounds like Dottore's style to me.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Careful!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Mmph... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (It's getting harder and harder to use my power...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Phew... Time to go. I wonder where I'll find myself this time?
